# cycles-vs-eevee-decision (reference summary)

## Purpose
Pick Cycles, Eevee, or Workbench for a render based on quality bar, time budget, and feature requirements (caustics, subsurface, etc.). Note: Eevee was named Eevee Next on Blender 4.2-4.x only.

Pick the render engine upfront based on quality + time tradeoff and feature requirements. Avoid the "use Cycles always" / "Eevee is faster" oversimplifications.

## Metadata & truth boundary
- **Canonical skill:** `skills/cycles-vs-eevee-decision/SKILL.md`
- **Contract:** `skills/cycles-vs-eevee-decision/contract.json` (`v1.0.0`)
- **Category / role:** `render-and-output-decisions` / `render-engine-tradeoff-selector`
- **Capability tier:** `L0`
- **Truth-state policy:** Runtime status defaults to `Not Run`; Artifact status defaults to `Not Produced`; mutation rule is `downgrade_only` (never upgrade without verified evidence).

## When to use
- before render
- when feature support drives engine choice
- when time vs quality tradeoff matters
- when previous render was wrong engine

## Trigger cues
- "Cycles or Eevee"
- "what render engine"
- "is Eevee enough"
- "render is too slow"

## When not to use
- for a known repeat render (engine already chosen) → delegate to `blender-lighting-material-planner` (`references/skills/blender-lighting-material-planner.md`; engine already chosen)
- for non-render work (modeling / animation prep) → delegate to `output-format-decision` (`references/skills/output-format-decision.md`; modeling / animation prep)

## Inputs & output/evidence contract
### Required inputs
- `deliverable_use_case` (`string`): Whether the output is a final hero still, lookdev preview, animation turntable, or baked GLB source
- `optical_feature_requirements` (`array`): Required optical features (refraction, caustics, Volumetrics, SSS, soft area shadows)
- `render_time_and_hardware_budget` (`string`): Per-frame render time ceiling and available GPU/CPU compute posture

### Optional inputs
- `blender_version_token` (`string`): Target Blender version governing BLENDER_EEVEE vs BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT naming

### Primary outputs
- `selected_render_engine_record`
- `sample_and_denoiser_targets`
- `engine_tradeoff_and_fallback_caveats`

## Quick-start procedure
1. Name the use case (hero / preview / animation / lookdev / flat clay).
2. Evaluate required rendering features (caustics / subsurface scattering / volumetrics / global illumination accuracy).
3. Evaluate time budget per frame and available hardware.
4. Pick the engine: `Cycles`, `Eevee`, or `Workbench` (note: Eevee used the name Eevee Next and token `BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT` on Blender 4.2–4.x only; it is `Eevee` with token `BLENDER_EEVEE` on 4.0–4.1 and 5.x).
5. Pin the 4-item engine record: engine + samples + GPU device (if applicable) + caveats.

## Safety boundaries & non-goals
- **Runtime boundary:** Decision skill — does not run Blender. Pins config; operator applies in scene render properties.
- Never run Blender or execute a render or preview render.
- Never configure denoiser specifics, tile sizes, light probe volumes, or render-setting optimizations beyond `engine + samples + GPU device + caveats`.
- Never decide color management (`color-management-decision`), container/codec (`output-format-decision`), or resolution/aspect (`resolution-aspect-decision`).
- Never verify rendered files (`render-export-evidence`).
